facts.text: simple/FrankaTabletopGraspMP-v0 is registered with entry point simple.envs.tabletop_grasp:TabletopGraspEnv and task franka_tabletop_grasp_mp
BaseDualSim defaults sim_mode to mujoco_isaac and always builds MuJoCo; a mode without 'isaac' sets the Isaac Sim simulator to None
The environment takes action_space and observation_space from the task
The task's action_space is the robot controller's action space
The controller action space is a Dict with one 'arm' entry
The arm PD joint-position controller is configured with joint1 to joint7
Each arm joint action is bounded by -1.0 and 1.0
The Franka Research 3 robot has 9 degrees of freedom
The parallel gripper is configured with the two finger joints finger_joint1 and finger_joint2
_get_obs returns agent, joint_qpos and eef_pose and merges the rendered camera frames into the observation
The observation space bounds agent and joint_qpos to -pi..pi with robot.dof entries and eef_pose to -inf..inf with 7 entries, and adds the camera spaces of the task sensor configs
The task configures a 640x360 front stereo camera, a 480x270 wrist camera, a 480x270 second wrist camera and a 640x360 side camera
The task metadata defaults physics_dt to 0.002 s and render_hz to 30
MujocoSimulator reads physics_dt from the task metadata
MujocoSimulator reads need_gravity from the task metadata and defaults it to False
MujocoSimulator sets the MuJoCo model timestep to physics_dt
Without need_gravity, MujocoSimulator.step advances MuJoCo from the current physics time to the end of the next render frame (render_step + 1) / render_hz using the model timestep
reset calls task.reset(seed, options), updates the MuJoCo layout, steps it once, clears step_count and _success, and returns the observation and info
step applies the action, steps MuJoCo, increments step_count, computes the reward and success, never truncates, and returns obs, reward, terminated, truncated and info
The task reward is clip((target height - initial target height) / _LIFT_HEIGHT, 0, 1)
_LIFT_HEIGHT is 0.02 m
check_success returns reward >= 1.0
Task.reset seeds the domain randomizer with dr.reset(seed=seed) unless an option carries a state_dict
close closes the MuJoCo simulator and the Isaac Sim application if it was loaded, then calls gym.Env.close

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the domain randomisation and the fake's initial jitter, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the fake draws initial values with Python's random.Random while the upstream task seeds numpy-based domain randomisers, so a seed gives different worlds on the two

gaps: rigid-body dynamics and contacts are those of the MuJoCo model built from the task layout; no actuator, sensor or noise model is claimed, and the fake backend is not the MuJoCo engine
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0; an OpenMHS tick is one env.step and the fake advances one placeholder control step per tick

control period: the physics timestep is 2 ms (the task's physics_dt, set on the MuJoCo model), while one env.step advances MuJoCo to the end of the next render frame at render_hz 30 (about 16-17 physics steps, a control period of about 33.3 ms); timestep_ms names the physics timestep per FID-015 and the package has no operating_notes field, so the control period is disclosed here
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

the fake is a pure Python kinematic stand-in: it implements only the scalar observation members agent, joint_qpos and eef_pose, not the camera images the upstream _get_obs returns through _render_frame; the real camera observations are 640x360 for front_stereo_left, front_stereo_right and side_left and 480x270 for wrist and wrist_left

the upstream package needs Python 3.10, MuJoCo 3.3.6, IsaacSim 4.5 and an RTX GPU (pyproject.toml, README.md); it was not installed or run where the gate ran, so the fake was not compared with the upstream environment
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
the fake's step, jitter and pose constants are placeholders, not calibrated values; only the reward shape and the success threshold follow the task code cited in the facts

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the last observation and the fake state are kept and stay readable
